story_pergunta: At your company, who checks what the AI agent actually did?

slides.eyebrow: AI ON THE RISE · AI AGENTS
slides.headline: The best AI agents still fail a third of everyday tasks
slides.sub: A new benchmark tests agents on real work, not demos.

slides.headline: ShellBench tested agents on the messy work people actually delegate
slides.body: TechCrunch reports that even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta failed more than a third of the time. The benchmark draws on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world agent interactions.

slides.label: of attempts recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments
slides.sub: Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed a safety requirement.

slides.headline: What I see in companies: the demo works, the real task doesn't
items: The agent gets access to messy data, and nobody defined what it may touch
Nobody approves the action before it has a side effect
The team ships it and never measures how often it fails

slides.headline: A multi-agent platform in production at an enterprise account
items: A US$5.5 million account running a multi-agent platform in production
About 60% efficiency gain on the work the agents handle
Multi-agent in production requires an audited defect log

slides.headline: Measure instead of assuming.
slides.body: In practice, the fix is not waiting for a better model. The article itself shows results shift with the harness around the model. Scoped tools, approvals and a log of every defect tell you what the agent really does.

slides.eyebrow: WANT TO SEE HOW I DID IT?
slides.headline: Comment AGENTS.
slides.body: I'll send you the step-by-step of this case by DM. I take AI off the drawing board and put it into production, with measured results.

caption:
A new benchmark called ShellBench tested AI agents on everyday work. According to TechCrunch, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement. In one task, agents recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments 40.3% of the time.

What I see in companies is the same gap. The demo looks great. Then the agent meets real data, real permissions and real consequences. Nobody defined what it can touch, nobody approves the risky step, and nobody measures failures.

That is the problem I work on. I run a multi-agent platform in production at an enterprise account, a US$5.5 million account, with about 60% efficiency gain. Multi-agent in production requires an audited defect log. In practice, the model is only one part. Scoped tools, approvals and measurement are what make it usable.

Launching is not the same as being used. Measure instead of assuming.

Comment AGENTS and I'll DM you how I did it.

Sources: techcrunch.com, huggingface.co
